title: Fix cmd/guard fuzz-runner flake: worker start/finish failures misclassified as crashes
objective: Make the cmd/guard fuzz check deterministic under resource pressure: a Go fuzz worker that fails to start, communicate, or terminate must not be classified as a target crash, while genuine crashes and timeouts must still be reported.
nonGoals: no change to the bounded fuzz budget or fuzztime default
no suppression of genuine crash or timeout findings
nextAction: reproduce under ulimit -n 64, make the classifier distinguish worker infrastructure failure from a target crash, and pin both behaviours with tests
notes: Opened 2026-10-01 by PM from the FJ-041 cleaner reproduction. The classifier treats any '--- FAIL: <Target>' line as a crash, which includes Go's own worker start/communication/termination failures under load, and fuzzOutput.truncated is never consulted.

Reproduction: bash -c 'ulimit -n 64; go test ./cmd/guard -run TestRunFuzzPass -count=1 -v' -> 'guard.fuzz.crash p/fuzz_p_test.go 5 fuzz target FuzzSafe failed'. 32 load-only invocations did not trigger it, so it is environment-triggered rather than constant.
Impact: a spurious guard.fuzz.failed row makes ./scripts/verify-candidate exit non-zero for an unrelated candidate, which blocks any ticket coincidentally verified under the same pressure.
